tables.heading_context: ## Layer 3a: In-Place Storage — Heap and B-tree Files
rows: O(log_b n), b = keys per page (large, ~hundreds)
A billion rows is ~3–4 levels deep
3–4 page touches, often all cached but the leaf
O(log_b n) to find start + sequential leaf walk
Leaves room for in-place inserts; trades space

tables.heading_context: ## The Amplification Triangle — the universal trade-off
rows: physical bytes written ÷ logical bytes written
Low at ingest, but **compaction** rewrites data many times over its life
Higher — check memtable + multiple levels (Bloom filters mitigate)
Tunable — tombstones + stale versions until compaction; leveled vs tiered changes this
The **buffer pool**, but DB-managed with knowledge of access patterns
A table with no index = full scan
Clustered index = the table; InnoDB always
Log-append then compact (like a GC'd allocator)
Azure Cosmos/Cassandra-API uses LSM under the hood
Transaction log flush before COMMIT ack
Read-heavy OLTP, point + range lookups on indexed keys
Write-heavy ingest, time-series, log/event data, SSD
You need cheap, predictable point reads above all
B+tree — single descent, no Bloom-filter misses
You need maximum sustained write throughput
LSM with size-tiered compaction (accept space + read amp)
Disk space is the binding constraint
LSM **leveled** compaction (low space amp) or compress B-tree pages
"Why did my delete not free space?"
LSM tombstones — space reclaimed only at compaction
"Why is COMMIT slower than the write?"
WAL flush gating COMMIT (guide 06), not the page write
B+tree — linked leaves give sequential I/O
